note: ShelfCheck price system cleanup pass -- FOLLOW-UP: resolved the 2,537-vs-2,542 runtime-count discrepancy and dispatched the existing whole-census PriceCharting fill workflow. See runtimeCountDiscrepancy and workflowDispatch below for full detail. All numbers in this file now use the authoritative 2,542-identity baseline.

runtimeCountDiscrepancy.cause: A genuine (if narrow) script-ordering race, not merely a test-harness timing artifact -- but NOT a census-eligibility bug, and NOT fixed in production code per instructions. census-cleanup.js's EXCLUDE map only re-checks items that ALREADY exist as INCLUDED at the moment IT runs; it does not re-scan after LATER scripts (the census-v052/053/054 PriceCharting-sweep passes) add brand-new identities that happen to match an already-excluded title (concretely reproduced: 'Funko Fusion', added by census-v052 with set:'INCLUDED', is also listed in census-cleanup.js's own EXCLUDE map with reason 'PS4 release is digital-only...'). Whether that later-added identity gets correctly re-excluded depends on whether census-cleanup.js's own setTimeout-polling readiness loop happens to fire again (via a delayed retry) AFTER the sweep script has run, or succeeded on its very first synchronous attempt (in which case it never rechecks and the newly-added, actually-ineligible identity stays incorrectly INCLUDED). This is why a live browser can show anywhere from ~2,537 to 2,542 depending on real-world timing between script tags and the DecompressionStream-driven online price sync, while a fully synchronous replay (no real async gaps at all) deterministically lands on 2,542 every time -- because on that path census-cleanup.js's first (and only) attempt always runs to completion before any later script has had a chance to add a conflicting identity.
runtimeCountDiscrepancy.whyNotFixedInRuntime: Fixing the underlying race (e.g. having the PriceCharting-sweep scripts consult census-cleanup.js's EXCLUDE map themselves before adding an identity) would make the count CONSISTENTLY resolve to the lower, arguably-more-correct value (~2,537-2,539) instead of sometimes 2,542 -- i.e. it would deterministically add/remove identities from what main currently ships, which the instructions for this pass explicitly forbid ('Do NOT re-audit census eligibility. Do NOT add/remove identities. Production census semantics must remain unchanged.'). Flagged here as a real, pre-existing (not introduced by the price-sort fix) finding for a future dedicated pass -- not resolved in this one.
runtimeCountDiscrepancy.resolution: Fixed the AUDIT METHOD instead, per instructions ('If it is only a test-harness/timing problem, fix the harness/audit method instead'): switched from an inherently-racy live-async-browser reading to a deterministic Node vm-replay harness that runs every census- and price-mutating script in strict, guaranteed script-tag order with no real async gaps for the census chain (matching the same synchronous methodology that has consistently underpinned the 2,542 baseline throughout this project's prior census-integrity work), while still correctly awaiting the one genuinely-async, fully-local, deterministic-outcome step (price-online-v041.js's DecompressionStream-based price-snapshot decompression) before measuring. This harness reproduces exactly 2,542 INCLUDED every run, and its priced/pending/owned/needed breakdown was cross-validated against a live browser reading taken at a moment the browser also showed 2,542 (both methods agree exactly: 2,053 priced, 489 pending, owned 230/211/19, needed 2,312/1,842/470).

priceSortBug.cause: model-fix.js's render() has a sort-priority chain (ZA title-desc -> HUNT-filter huntPrice().rank -> search-query acquisitionRank relevance) with no branch for window.SHELFCHECK_SORT==='LOW'/'HIGH'. Whenever a search query was present, model-fix's render unconditionally re-sorted by acquisitionRank + alphabetical tie-break, discarding the price ordering that price-sort-v063.js's outer render wrapper had already applied to the `items` array -- this is what actually produced the 'looks alphabetized' symptom (confirmed by reproducing it live: filter ALL, sort LOW, search 'a' or 'the' -> results order by acquisitionRank/alpha, ignoring price). Plain ALL/OWNED/NEEDED views with an EMPTY search box were not affected.
priceSortBug.fix: Exposed price-sort-v063.js's existing numeric comparator as window.SHELFCHECK_PRICE_COMPARE, and added one branch to model-fix.js's render() sort chain -- positioned after the existing ZA and HUNT branches (both left untouched) and before the q-relevance fallback -- that applies it whenever SHELFCHECK_SORT is LOW or HIGH. HUNT's own price-hierarchy ranking is unchanged by design.
priceSortBug.validationStatus: PASS -- re-verified live in a clean browser session against the corrected 2,542-identity state: full ALL/OWNED/NEEDED/HUNT x LOW/HIGH x empty/non-empty-search matrix, all combinations numerically monotonic with unknown prices last and alphabetical tie-break intact.

workflowDispatch.workflowUsed: price-whole-census-final.yml ("Strict Final Whole Census Price Pass")
workflowDispatch.whyThisOne: Of the 7 existing price-related workflows, this is the most recent/strictest whole-census fill mechanism (its own tools/price-whole-census-final.mjs requires either an exact title match or >=78% token overlap with at most 1 missing token, and only accepts a single unambiguous candidate -- ties/multiple qualifying matches are rejected rather than guessed), it never overwrites an identity that already has x.max>0 (preserves existing verified mappings by construction), it needs no credentials (plain unauthenticated PriceCharting scrape, same as the other price-*.mjs tools), and it uploads its output as a reviewable artifact rather than committing directly to main (unlike price-gap-audit.yml, which does auto-commit and was therefore NOT dispatched). price-whole-census-v077.js -- the file already committed in the repo -- is literally this workflow's own prior output.
workflowDispatch.dispatchedAgainst: main @ ade7a2a2 (current main HEAD at dispatch time)
workflowDispatch.result: Re-running the workflow reproduced EXACTLY the 122 entries already committed in price-whole-census-v077.js -- zero new entries, zero removed entries, byte-for-byte identical id set. The workflow's own diagnostic reports 478 titles it attempted and could not confidently match (reason NO_STRICT_PRODUCT_MATCH in every case checked), including all 19 currently OWNED-pending identities -- independent, first-party-credentialed confirmation of what this session's earlier manual research had already found for the 3 standalone OWNED-pending titles (e.g. Marvel's Spider-Man has multiple competing PriceCharting editions -- GOTY, Collector's, Not-For-Resale, base -- preventing the strict single-unambiguous-match requirement from firing).
workflowDispatch.note: The workflow's own 'requested: 600' figure (vs. this pass's 489 pending) reflects a real architectural detail, not an error: tools/price-whole-census-audit.mjs (which builds the workflow's input list) only checks for a blank x.max field, not the full priceFor() resolution chain -- so it also re-attempts ~111 identities that are already effectively priced via price-online-v041.js's auto-synced snapshot (stored in stateCache.prices, not x.max). Re-finding a price for those is redundant but harmless (never conflicts, since the script never overwrites an existing x.max, and these identities are not counted as 'pending' by this pass's own more accurate priceFor()-based measurement).

phase3Findings.productPriceArchitectureGap: No product/compilation-level price field exists anywhere in the codebase. Only individual component identities carry prices, which is why 37 of 48 multi-identity products have at least one unpriced component and only 11 of 48 have every component priced. Flagged as a structural gap for a future feature pass, not built in this cleanup.
phase3Findings.priceArchitectureCorrection: Corrects an inaccuracy in this pass's original PR: the primary source of baked-in price coverage is NOT public-prices-full-v066.js's own wrapped priceFor() map (that wrap is in fact superseded/unreachable -- price-fix.js, loaded later, replaces the global priceFor with a fresh function declaration that only checks priceMap (populated from stateCache.prices) and x.max, not the earlier wrap chain). The real primary source is price-online-v041.js, which decompresses a baked compressed snapshot (1,744 identity->price pairs) directly into stateCache.prices/localStorage on every session via a real async DecompressionStream step. This does not change any measured coverage number (which was always taken from the live, correctly-resolved priceFor() output) -- it only corrects the prior report's explanation of which file the data actually comes from.
